+# Postmortem
+
+## Root Cause
+A recent commit ("Order library list by shelf position", hash 53c6202) changed the books API endpoint to load all books into memory using `.all()` and then sorting them in Python, rather than using database-level sorting and pagination. This caused a massive performance regression, leading to the P99 HTTP request latency on the `booklogr-api` service exceeding the 300ms threshold (spiking to 1.225s).
+
+## Evidence Used
+- Alerting Stack: Alert `BooklogrApiLatencyP99High` fired indicating p99 HTTP request latency was 1.225s.
+- Git log: Investigated recent commits and found 53c6202 ("Order library list by shelf position").
+- Code analysis: Reviewed the diff for commit 53c6202 and observed that database-level `order_by()` and `paginate()` were replaced by an inefficient application-level `sorted(books.all())`, which retrieves all database rows into memory.
+
+## What was changed
+Reverted the sorting and pagination logic in `api/routes/books.py` back to using SQLAlchemy's `order_by()` and `paginate()`, removing the application-level `sorted(books.all())` logic.
